additional_axis_disorder.physics_result: GHOST ZERO DESTROYED by axis disorder. Unlike Cartan c-disorder (which preserves QCMI=0 at p=0.5), axis direction perturbations break the x_hat alignment condition, causing QCMI > 0 even at p=0.5. This CONFIRMS the theoretical expectation: the ghost zero requires ALL Cartan axes = x_hat. c-disorder is a 'soft' perturbation (preserves the ghost manifold), while axis disorder is a 'hard' perturbation (destroys it).

synthesis.primary_verdict: HARRIS MARGINAL: alpha shows a small but statistically significant drift with disorder strength W (slope = 0.0130 +/- 0.0003, range/mean = 0.0034). The ghost zero is NEARLY robust to c-disorder but not perfectly so — disorder is WEAKLY RELEVANT. This PARTIALLY WEAKENS the MBL analogy: the ghost zero is not a true infinite-randomness fixed point, but rather a finite-disorder critical point with slow RG flow of the disorder strength.
synthesis.secondary_verdict: TOPOLOGY-DEPENDENT confirmed. Vertex chain (rings) alpha=1.8320 vs path (no rings) alpha=1.8417 differ by 0.0098 (9.3 sigma). The ghost zero scaling exponent is NOT fully universal — it depends on graph structure. Specifically, the presence of CLOSED LOOPS (rings) in the vertex chain REDUCES alpha compared to the open path graph. Rings create interference paths that enhance entanglement production at small |dp|, lowering the effective exponent. Star graph shows alpha varying with |E| (b1-dep), suggesting finite-size effects dominate when the system qubit count is fixed at 1.
synthesis.tertiary_verdict: Data collapse within each |E| is EXCELLENT (std/mean < 3%). Cross-|E| collapse is MODERATE (quality=0.191) because the amplitude A(|E|) scales linearly with |E|: QCMI ~ |E| * |dp|^alpha. The correction-to-scaling exponent omega ~ 0.14-0.17 characterizes deviations from pure power-law at finite |dp|. A FULL collapse is achieved with: QCMI / (|E| * |dp|^alpha) = const.
synthesis.axis_disorder_verdict: GHOST ZERO DESTROYED by axis disorder. Unlike Cartan c-disorder (which preserves QCMI=0 at p=0.5), axis direction perturbations break the x_hat alignment condition, causing QCMI > 0 even at p=0.5. This CONFIRMS the theoretical expectation: the ghost zero requires ALL Cartan axes = x_hat. c-disorder is a 'soft' perturbation (preserves the ghost manifold), while axis disorder is a 'hard' perturbation (destroys it).

key_numerical_results.topology_verdict: TOPOLOGY-INDEPENDENT — alpha is universal across graph structures

implications: DISORDER is WEAKLY RELEVANT: alpha drifts +0.006 over W=[0,0.5] (37 sigma slope). Ghost zero is NEARLY robust but not perfectly — MBL analogy PARTIALLY SUPPORTED.
TOPOLOGY MATTERS: Vertex chain (rings) vs path (no rings) alpha differs by 0.010 (9.3 sigma). Closed loops REDUCE alpha (enhance entanglement at small |dp|).

AXIS DISORDER DESTROYS GHOST ZERO: unlike c-disorder, axis perturbations break the x_hat alignment and cause QCMI > 0 even at p=0.5. This is expected theoretically and confirms the ghost zero requires ALL axes = x_hat.
Star graph alpha varies with |E|: when |S|=1 fixed, finite-size effects dominate.
Data collapse within each |E| is excellent; cross-|E| needs |E|-scaling factor.
Correction-to-scaling exponent omega ~ 0.15 provides first subleading ghost zero characterization.
open_questions: Is alpha(W) drift a finite-size artifact (only b1=2 tested) or a genuine RG flow?
Can the alpha vs topology relationship be derived from graph Laplacian spectra?
Is there a functional form alpha(b1, graph structure) that classifies all ghost zero universality classes?
Does the correction exponent omega have a universal value across topologies?
Can the ghost zero be stabilized against axis disorder by adding symmetry protection?
synthesis.confidence: HIGH for topology comparison and axis disorder physics; MEDIUM for disorder Harris criterion (only b1=2 tested, needs b1=1,3 confirmation)
